newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JUNE 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - JUNE 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Manufacturing is coming to the rescue of a faltering economy as producers go for exports, with output soaring to a record high in April.

- Inkatha Freedom Party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi was likely to play a role in foreign affairs if he accepted the post of second deputy president for the remaining years of the government of national unity, African National Congress sources said.

- The KWV wine cooperative has admitted it might have been involved in a plan to sell thousands of cases of South African sparkling wine disguised as French champagne and is investigating the allegations.
- Cellular telephone company Vodacom and rival MTN appear set for a legal clash after the announcement of a 100 million rand golf sponsorship deal.
- Former housing director-general Billy Cobbett and the government have agreed on the terms of his departure from office.

- An academic has proposed far-reaching steps to strengthen industrial policy, including a change in the Reserve Bank's monetary policy and proposing that the government pay more attention to the role of conglomerates in determining industrial policy.
- South Africa has reached an interim agreement with China on measures guaranteeing unrestricted access for business and holiday travellers to Hong Kong, the foreign affairs department said.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority has rapped Telkom on the knuckles over its bid to monopolise access to the Internet.

- Nick Barnardt, strategic economist at BoE NatWest, says South Africa should copy Britain and have the government of the day set inflation targets and leave decisions on interest rates to a committee in the central bank, guided by the politicians' inflation target.
- The South African Air Force has hired an outside firm to maintain 17 VIP and utility transport aircraft.
- Food group Choice Holdings reported a taxed loss of 90 million rand for the year to February 28.

- SAA's [SAA.CN] Voyager frequent flyer incentive programme has been criticised for avoiding giving passengers the air miles they deserve, because of a complex system of ticket price increases and discounts.
SAKE-BEELD

- Black economic empowerment was given a hefty boost with the formation of a new company, City Press Media (Pty) Ltd, through which black business groups will take a 40 percent stake in the City Press Sunday paper.
- The Mineworkers' Union, the only labour union in the country which limits its membership to whites, has amended its constitution to bring it in line with the Labour Relations Act.
- South Africa climbed 10 places this year on the international list of countries with the highest human development. It moved up to 90th in the list of 175 countries.
THE STAR
- The heaviest snowfall in years cut off three southern KwaZulu-Natal towns from the outside world, leaving hundreds of motorists trapped in their cars.
- More than 1,000 staff will leave the South African Broadcasting Corp by month-end, having either resigned or accepted voluntary severance packages. A further 400 face possible forced lay-offs.
- A schoolteacher became an instant hero when he shot and killed two hijackers who tried to take his car.
THE CITIZEN
- Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma denied she had bowed to pressure by withdrawing three controversial health bills.
- An 11-year-old girl was in a stable condition in hospital after three hijackers shot her in the chest as her mother was driving her to school.
- A motorist was shot and killed by a gunman who took his car, but abandoned it a few kilometres away.
